summary: Created a `remove-nul-files` command on PATH (a Node.js script plus a .cmd shim in `C:\Users\mchan\.pi\agent\bin`) that recursively removes case-insensitive `NUL` files under the home directory without following symlinks, and ran it to delete 8 existing NUL files. Then created two private GitHub repositories (`mcread29/gizmo-registry` and `mcread29/gizmo-skills-registry`), pushed the existing local registry contents to them, pointed `installed.json` at the GitHub URLs, and committed and pushed the leftover `ChangesPanel` changes in `gizmo-registry` (commit `fa038ec`).
decisions: Installed the NUL remover as `remove-nul-files` in `C:\Users\mchan\.pi\agent\bin` (already on PATH) using a `.mjs` script wrapped by a `.cmd` shim so it works as a bare command.

The NUL scanner does not follow directory symlinks (checks `!entry.isSymbolicLink()`) and counts unscannable directories as `skipped` rather than `failed`, exiting 0 as long as at least one root was readable.

Hosting the two Gizmo registries as private repos on GitHub under `mcread29/`, switching their tracked `origin` from the local managed copies to the GitHub URLs (HTTPS in installed.json, SSH in git remotes).
Bumped the installed registry manifest's recorded commit for `gizmo-registry` to `fa038ec` after the `refine changes panel rendering` commit was pushed.
errors: Initial `remove-nul-files --dry-run` exited with code 1 because inaccessible directories were counted as failures; after changing them to a `skipped` count with `console.warn`, the real run exited 0.
`C:\Users\mchan\AppData\Local\ElevatedDiagnostics` could not be scanned (EPERM); handled by the skip path and reported as 'Skipped 1 inaccessible directory'.
